engine_name: Healthy Weight Check: BMI with NICE NG246 categories (lower thresholds for South Asian, Chinese, other Asian, Middle Eastern, Black African and African-Caribbean family backgrounds), waist-to-height ratio bands, healthy weight range for height, and a safety layer that stops before any number for under-18s, pregnancy or breastfeeding and eating disorders
intended_use: Free educational check for adults that shows BMI, waist-to-height ratio and a healthy weight range for height, with plain guidance. It does not diagnose any condition, set a weight target or give calorie advice.
eligibility: Adults aged 18 to 99. Stops with an owner-approved message and no numbers for under-18s, pregnancy or breastfeeding (including 'not sure') and a current, past or suspected eating disorder (D52). Unintended weight loss shows a see-your-doctor banner above the result.
sources: NICE guideline NG246 (2025), Overweight and obesity management, recommendations 1.9.7 to 1.9.15: BMI categories, lower thresholds for listed family backgrounds, waist-to-height ratio 0.4-0.49 / 0.5-0.59 / 0.6 or more for BMI under 35. https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng246
Ashwell M, Gibson S. Waist-to-height ratio as an indicator of early health risk. BMJ Open 2016;6:e010159.
limitations: BMI is a screening measure; less reliable for older adults, very muscular people, after limb loss and in pregnancy (not used).
Category and band follow the rounded value shown (D55); the obesity class 2 and 3 thresholds for adjusted backgrounds use NICE's 2.5 reduction.
The Daily Protein Target and the Diabetes Risk Check keep their frozen, older cut-offs (D56); the difference is explained in this tool's method section.
regulatory_statement: Pending the owner's clinical sign-off (FR2-39 AS-19). General health information, not a diagnosis or a medical device.
licence: Lifeline Daily's own implementation of published NICE thresholds.
